reports.title: The Trial of Russell Brand | Day 20: “Nobody is above the law”
reports.description:

reports.title: How does the jury decide? | The Trial of Russell Brand Ep. 18
reports.description:
On the 18th day of the trial of Russell Brand, we join Times Crime Correspondent Jess Sharkey outside Southwark Crown Court as she waits for a verdict. 
Not knowing when that verdict will come, Jess is sitting in a corridor all day waiting for the moment when a voice comes over the loud speakers, calling her into the courtroom.
In the meantime, while the court was on its lunch break, we took the opportunity to ask her some listener questions: why has this trial been so short? Does the verdict really have to be unanimous? And what happens if the twelve jurors can’t agree?
Russell Brand denies all the allegations against him.

reports.title: “Poisoning of the well” | The Trial of Russell Brand Ep. 16
reports.description:
On the 16th day of the trial of Russell Brand, the defence delivered their closing statement.
The defence argued media reports in 2023 had “poisoned the well” against Brand, causing women to “reimagine” consensual sexual encounters and come forward to make complaints to police. Ian Winter KC also argued the time taken for these women to come forward was a “corrupter of justice” and there was no reasonable explanation for the delay.
Russell Brand denies all the allegations against him.

reports.title: “Half-truths spun into lies” | The Trial of Russell Brand Ep. 15
reports.description:
On the 15th day of the trial of Russell Brand, the prosecution delivered their closing statement to the jury.
Riel Karmy-Jones, the lead barrister for the prosecution, emphasised the complainants are six women who do not know each other, and have not sought compensation or the limelight.
She described Russell Brand’s evidence as “half-truths spun into lies”, and suggested his account had been “wholly constructed” from the prosecution case.
The defence will deliver their closing statement on Monday.
Russell Brand denies all the allegations against him.

reports.title: Brand's wife gives evidence | The Trial of Russell Brand Ep. 14
reports.description:
On the 14th day of the trial of Russell Brand, the wife of the comedian and christian influencer, Laura Brand, gave evidence. She told the court it was “clear it was hard for him to be monogamous” when the pair began dating in 2006, causing them to break up in 2007. After getting back together and marrying in 2017, she said Brand was “caring, kind” and “a wonderful father to our children.”
In cross-examination, the prosecution highlighted Laura Brand did not know the comedian during the time period relating to 5 of the counts.
Two former girlfriends of Russell Brand also provided statements as character witnesses.
Russell Brand denies all the allegations against him.

reports.title: Brand gives evidence | The Trial of Russell Brand Ep. 13
reports.description:
On episode 13 of the Trial of Russell Brand podcast, Russell Brand gave evidence for the first time.
Brand’s defence went through the details of each alleged offence, which relate to six women. The comedian told the court two of the allegations of rape were actually consensual sex. He said a third alleged rape did not happen. Consent, Brand insisted, was “fundamental… more important than sex itself”.
During cross-examination, the prosecution repeatedly asked why Brand hadn’t mentioned some of the details he gave in court during his earlier police interviews. 
Brand said “there’s been escalating recollection”. He denies all the allegations against him.
Rosamund Urwin and Charlotte Wace are in court every day, and then join Luke Jones to unpack it all.

reports.title: Invented, reimagined | The Trial of Russell Brand Ep. 12
reports.description:
On the twelfth day of the trial of Russell Brand, the jury were directed to find the defendant not guilty on one count of indecent assault. The judge, Justice Bennathan, told the jury there was insufficient evidence for count 2. This is where Brand was alleged to have grabbed the arm of a woman in the offices of MTV and attempted to drag her into a toilet.
However, a new count of “attempted indecent assault” was introduced in relation to the same incident.
The court also heard the prosecution read the prepared statements Russell Brand gave police when he was initially interviewed. In those statements the former comedian suggested complainants had “invented” allegations or “reimagined” consensual sexual encounters, after what he called “fictitious and defamatory” reporting in the press.
Russell Brand denies all the allegations against him.
Rosamund Urwin and Charlotte Wace are in court every day, and then join Luke Jones to unpack it all.
